byCountry.description: Aliases offered pre-checked to a new participant, by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

otherwise.description: The same, for every country not in byCountry.

customizationId.description: What a document of this type states in cbc:CustomizationID.

profileId.description: What a document of this type states in cbc:ProfileID.

shortName.description: What a person calls it, for a title.

structured.description: false: the canonical document model does not read this type.

syntaxVersion.description: The part of documentTypeId after the customization: 2.1 for UBL, D16B for CII.

type.description: The alias, as POST /v1/messages and a capability take it.

validated.description: false: no validation artefacts, so a capability needs allowUnvalidated.

valid.description: null when validated is false: a type with no rules that its capability lets go unvalidated.

code.description: Stable; branch on it. An operation's x-errors lists the codes it answers.

requestId.description: This request's X-Request-Id (yours if you sent one, ours otherwise). Quote it to support.

retryable.description: true when the same request may succeed if sent again unchanged: 429 and 5xx, except 501 and VALIDATION_ERROR, which name a state that does not pass. false for every other 4xx, which fails the same way until the request or the account changes. Retry a send with the same Idempotency-Key.

nextCursor.description: Always present. Ask again with ?after= set to it.

layer.description: schema (the document is not valid UBL, so Schematron did not run) or schematron.

severity.description: fatal, error or warning. A fatal finding makes valid false.

deliveryUnconfirmed.description: An outbound SEND_FAILED document whose send outcome is unknown: the receiver may have it. Never resend it.

mlsEvents.description: The Message Level Status trail, oldest first. GET /v1/messages/{id} only.

payload.description: The business document, on GET /v1/messages/{id} only while it is under the inline limit.

recipientStatus.description: CONFIRMED, DELIVERED or REJECTED, from the receiving Service Provider's MLS. Absent until one arrives.

type.description: The register alias for documentTypeId and processId; absent for a pair the register does not know.

validation.description: Which Peppol rules decided the validation status. GET /v1/messages/{id} only.

validationErrors.description: The findings of a failed validation, grouped. GET /v1/messages/{id} only.

effectiveFrom.description: When the release becomes mandatory, RFC 3339 UTC.

ruleset.description: The Peppol release, as GET /v1/validation/rulesets names it.

upcoming.description: The document checked against the release scheduled next; shown until it takes effect.

vesid.description: The exact validation artefacts the engine ran.

effectiveFrom.description: When the release takes effect; absent on one in force since before the platform recorded dates.
When the release becomes mandatory, RFC 3339 UTC.

headers.description: PUT the document to uploadUrl with exactly these headers.

count.description: How many times the finding occurred; 0 or absent means once.

id.description: The X-Peppol-Event-ID; the same on every delivery of the event and in GET /v1/events.

rules.description: message.outbound.ruleset_warning: the distinct rules it breaks there.

ruleset.description: message.outbound.ruleset_warning: the scheduled release the document would fail.

type.description: One of the six event types.

customerAuth.description: Customer session (pus_*) or API key (pap_*). X-API-Key is also accepted.

info.description: The customer API. Every endpoint here is reached with an API key or a user session, and answers only for the account that credential belongs to.
info.title: Business Gateway API

get.description: The account this credential belongs to, plus the companies it reaches. restricted is true for a credential confined to particular companies; such a credential reads the account's id, name and status only, because the remaining fields describe the account holder's own corporate identity and billing rather than anything about the companies under it. mfaRequired says whether the owner requires every user to hold a second factor (PATCH /v1/account).

patch.description: Owner only. Body {mfaRequired: true|false}: require every user of the account to hold a second factor — an authenticator app, a passkey they sign in with, or single sign-on. It applies from each user's next request: a password session of a user with neither is answered 403 MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED everywhere except GET /v1/me, their own PATCH /v1/users/{id}, POST /v1/mfa/enroll and /confirm, and the passkey registration routes; a password session of a user who has a passkey is answered 403 MFA_PASSKEY_SIGNIN_REQUIRED everywhere except GET /v1/me, since its only way out is signing in with that passkey. API keys and desk sessions are never affected. Turning it on answers 409 INVALID_STATE unless your own session already satisfies it; turning it off needs nothing. Answers {account}. 400 VALIDATION_FAILED without mfaRequired; 403 FORBIDDEN for anyone but an owner.

post.description: Owner only. Starts building a zip of everything the account holds: companies, participants, document metadata and payloads, and the audit trail. Returns {export: {id, status}}; poll GET .../export/{exportId} until it carries a download link. Large accounts take a while.

get.description: Owner only. {export: {id, status, downloadUrl?, expiresAt?, error?}}. downloadUrl is present only once status is DONE and within its 24h TTL.

Owner or company admin; an ordinary member is refused. Each key carries permissions: an array of read/send/receive/manage. A company admin sees only the keys confined to its own companies, never the account-wide ones. ?companyId narrows to one company; a key confined to no company reaches the whole account and stays in view whichever company is asked for.

post.description: Owner or company admin. companyId confines the key to one company; leaving it out produces a key that reaches every company under the account, which only an owner may create. permissions is an array of read/send/receive/manage; omitted or empty means all four. Calling a route the key lacks the permission for is 403 PERMISSION_DENIED. The key itself is in the response and is never shown again.

delete.description: Owner or company admin, the latter only for a key confined to one of its own companies. Revoking is immediate and cannot be undone.

post.description: {email}. Always 204, whether or not the address belongs to a user, so that the response cannot be used to discover who has an account.

{email, password}. Answers {token, expiresAt, user}. For a user with an authenticator app the password is only the first step: the answer also carries mfaRequired: true, and the token is a pending session that reaches nothing but POST /v1/auth/mfa. A user without one gets a full session, exactly as before.

Completes the pending session POST /v1/auth/login answers with mfaRequired: true when the user has an authenticator app (S-30). Bearer is that pending token; until this succeeds it is refused everywhere else with 403 MFA_REQUIRED, and it lapses after five minutes. Body {code}: a 6-digit code from the app or one of the unused recovery codes, each accepted once. Answers the login shape, {token, expiresAt, user}, with the same token now complete. 401 UNAUTHORIZED for a wrong code, 401 MFA_CHALLENGE_EXPIRED when the bearer is missing, unknown or lapsed (sign in again; the message text is unchanged), 409 INVALID_STATE when no challenge is outstanding (the session is complete, or the user's two-factor was turned off meanwhile), 429 RATE_LIMITED after repeated wrong codes.

Signs in with an OIDC token from the account's identity provider. 401 SSO_NOT_LINKED — distinct from the generic UNAUTHORIZED — means the token is valid but no user here is linked to it yet; link the identity after signing in with a password.

Unauthenticated. Returns {publicKey}, the options the browser passes to navigator.credentials.get(), with the challenge and every credential id base64url-encoded. The challenge is single-use and lives five minutes. allowCredentials is empty by design: passkeys here are discoverable, so the authenticator names the account and this route reveals nothing about who has one.

Unauthenticated: {id, authenticatorData, clientDataJSON, signature, userHandle}, all base64url. Returns the same {token, expiresAt, user} a password login does. Every verification failure is one 401 UNAUTHORIZED, except 401 PASSKEY_CLONE_DETECTED — the authenticator's signature counter went backwards, and the passkey should be removed rather than retried.

{token, password}. A token that is unknown, expired, already used, or whose user can no longer sign in is 400 RESET_TOKEN_INVALID — its own code, so a client can offer a fresh link without reading the message.

Creates an account (the contract party), its first company (the account's own legal entity unless a company object says otherwise) and the first owner: {account:{name?,legalName,countryCode,registrationNumber?,vatNumber?}, company?:{name?,identifier?,countryCode?,registrationNumber?,vatNumber?}, owner:{name?,email,password}, bootstrapToken?}.

get.description: What the account's companies cost, per month. Answers the owner, a user holding the billing.view grant (PATCH /v1/users/{id}) and a desk session; everyone else, every API key included, gets 403 FORBIDDEN. A user confined to some companies sees only those companies, and every month, line and total is summed over them alone (scope: "companies"). ?companyId narrows the report further to the companies named — repeated (?companyId=a&companyId=b) or comma-separated (?companyId=a,b) — and every month, line and total (yearToDate and sinceStart included) is then summed over those alone, with scope: "companies" and companyIds echoing the selection; an empty ?companyId= is no filter. It only narrows what the caller already sees: a company outside the caller's scope, or one that does not exist, is 404 NOT_FOUND, as on every customer route that takes a companyId. ?period=2026-09 or 2026-Q3, or ?from=2026-01&to=2026-09 (at most 120 months); with none of them, the year to date. months[] has one entry per month with state locked (frozen when the basis was taken out), draft (ended and measured, not yet locked), running (this month, counted live), unmeasured (ended before anything measured it: no numbers) or future, and companyMonths, participantMonths, messages, outboundMessages, inboundMessages, amountMinor, pricedAmountMinor and priceMissing. companies[] gives the same per company and per company and month; lines[] the period's price lines, unit price × quantity = amount. totals has period, yearToDate and sinceStart (from the first measured month), each with its from and to. Amounts are integer minor units of currency. A month without a price keeps its counts and has priceMissing: true with amountMinor null — never 0 — and so does every sum that includes it; pricedAmountMinor is the priced part. outboundMessages and inboundMessages are null where the split is not known (the metering rows behind an old month may have been archived), and always in the yearToDate and sinceStart totals. Sandbox companies are free and appear nowhere. ?format=csv gives one row per month and company: month,state,companyId,company,companyMonths,participantMonths,messages,outboundMessages,inboundMessages,amountMinor,amount,priceMissing,currency.

?q matches name, identifier, id, registration number and VAT number, case-insensitively. Without ?limit or ?cursor the whole matching list comes back at once; pass either and cursor pagination applies, with nextCursor set while more remains.

post.description: Owner, or an account-wide API key with manage. Adds a legal entity under the account. Empty countryCode inherits the account's; an omitted identifier is derived from the name. When the account is expected to do KYC the response carries onboarding: {url, expiresAt}, a hosted onboarding link to hand the company — see POST /v1/companies/{id}/kyc/onboarding-link. Participants under a company that has not completed KYC wait for operator approval. sandbox: true makes a sandbox company: its participants are local only (never on the Peppol network) and are created READY without operator approval, it gets no KYC onboarding link, and POST /v1/companies/{id}/test-inbound may simulate documents arriving at it; only an operator changes the flag afterwards.

delete.description: Owner, or an account-wide API key with manage — the same callers as POST and PATCH. Allowed once every participant of the company is DEACTIVATED (deactivate them with DELETE /v1/participants/{id} first), and always for a company that has none; otherwise 409 COMPANY_NOT_DEREGISTERED. The company is closed and its queued outbound and inbound are dropped (a close only pauses them; a deleted company cannot be reopened), its DEACTIVATED participants are deleted with it, API keys confined to it are revoked and SFTP logins confined to it disabled, and it frees its identifier for a new company. It then disappears from GET /v1/companies and every other list, and GET /v1/companies/{id} answers 404 — as does a second DELETE. The deletion is soft: documents, usage and billing keep naming the company, and audit records COMPANY_DELETED plus PARTICIPANT_DELETED per participant. 204 No Content.

patch.description: Owner, or an account-wide API key with manage. name, identifier (409 IDENTIFIER_TAKEN on collision), countryCode, registrationNumber, vatNumber. A company verified through KYC refuses a new registrationNumber or countryCode with 409 KYC_LOCKED. sandbox cannot be changed here.

get.description: The company's latest KYC case: {kyc: {id, status, method, source, orgNumber, legalName, persons, signatoryRule, signatures, requiresReview, companyVerified, ...}}. status is NOT_STARTED, PENDING_SIGNATURES, MANUAL_REVIEW, VERIFIED, REJECTED, EXPIRED or WITHDRAWN; a company that never started has only companyId, status, method, countryCode, required and companyVerified. required is false when the account is exempt from KYC: offer it as optional rather than as a step to finish. Nothing is blocked either way. method is "register" where a register extract is uploaded (Sweden: a Bolagsverket registreringsbevis) and "manual" elsewhere. companyVerified stays true while a newer case is in progress. 501 KYC_NOT_CONFIGURED when the deployment has no KYC.

post.description: Owner session only; an API key gets 403 KYC_USE_ONBOARDING_LINK. {objectKey} for a country with a register (method "register"), or {manual: {orgNumber, legalName, address?, signatoryText?}} for any other. A Swedish extract must be the PDF Bolagsverket issued, sealed by Bolagsverket over every byte and sealed within the last 90 days: 400 KYC_DOCUMENT_NOT_SEALED (no seal, or the file was changed after sealing — a scan or a re-saved copy), KYC_DOCUMENT_NOT_FROM_REGISTER, KYC_DOCUMENT_TOO_OLD, and KYC_ORG_NUMBER_MISMATCH when it is for another registration number than the company's. An authentic extract whose firmateckning cannot be read with confidence is accepted with requiresReview true. Starting a case ends any case still open; a verified company stays verified until the new case is. 400 KYC_MANUAL_REQUIRED for objectKey in a country without a register.

get.description: Owner, or an account-wide API key with manage. kind is agreement (the version the signatories were sent) or signed-agreement (that agreement followed by the signature appendix: who signed, when, from which address). From the case that verified the company, or else its latest case; 404 until there is one. The PDF comes back as an attachment with its SHA-256 in X-Content-SHA256, and the read is audited as KYC_DOCUMENT_READ.

post.description: Owner, or an account-wide API key with manage. Returns {onboarding: {url, expiresAt}}: a link, valid 30 days, that lets whoever holds it do the company's KYC on our hosted page — upload the registreringsbevis (or enter a foreign company), choose who signs — without an account here. Issuing one ends the previous link for the company. This is how a platform integrating through an API key gets its customers through KYC: the key itself is refused on the KYC routes with 403 KYC_USE_ONBOARDING_LINK.

Owner session only (an API key gets 403 KYC_USE_ONBOARDING_LINK), on a case in PENDING_SIGNATURES. With a signatory rule: {alternative, signers: [{personId, email}]}, where alternative indexes signatoryRule.alternatives (clauses naming individuals are listed in signatoryRule.notOffered and cannot be chosen) and the chosen persons must bind the company under it (400 KYC_SIGNATORIES_INSUFFICIENT otherwise). Without one (requiresReview): {signers: [{name, role?, email}]}. Every signer needs their own email address. Each gets a personal link valid 14 days; calling again replaces the earlier choice and ends its unsigned links, and someone who already signed is not asked again. 409 KYC_NO_AGREEMENT when no agreement version is published. When mail cannot be sent, unsentLinks carries the links to pass on another way.

Owner session only; an API key gets 403 KYC_USE_ONBOARDING_LINK. {size} in bytes, at most 5 MiB. Returns {objectKey, uploadUrl, expiresAt, headers}: PUT the PDF to uploadUrl with exactly the headers in headers (Content-Type: application/pdf) and a body of exactly size bytes (the URL is signed over both), then pass objectKey to POST /v1/companies/{id}/kyc. An upload not submitted within a day is deleted, and so is one that is refused; an accepted one is filed with the case.
post.summary: Upload URL for a register extract

post.description: Owner, or an account-wide API key with manage. For a company created with sandbox: true only (409 NOT_SANDBOX otherwise), in production as well. {receiver, sender?, type | documentTypeId+processId, payload, as4MessageId?}: the document runs the real inbound path — validation, storage, webhooks, pull — as a test injection (TEST_INBOUND_INJECTED). receiver must be one of this company's participants; a sandbox company's participants are always local, so a simulated document never shares a mailbox with a real one. Sender, receiver and type may be left out when the payload is an SBD that carries them. Rate limited per account.
post.summary: Simulate an inbound document to a sandbox company

post.description: Unauthenticated: a single-use handoff token is itself the credential. A reused or expired token is 401 UNAUTHORIZED.

get.description: Unauthenticated. Every document type the platform sends and receives, with the alias that names it on POST /v1/messages and in a capability (type), its labels, its family, both Peppol identifiers, and those identifiers already taken apart into what a document states: rootElement, rootNamespace, customizationId, profileId and syntaxVersion. validated is false for a type with no validation artefacts, whose capability needs allowUnvalidated; structured is false for a type the canonical model does not read. families is the display order, and defaults the types a new participant is offered pre-checked, per country with otherwise for every other country. The register is code, so the answer changes only with a deploy: it carries an ETag and Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, and If-None-Match with that ETag answers 304 Not Modified with no body. New types and new fields are additive.

Every event a webhook would carry, oldest first, kept 30 days, whether or not the account has a webhook. Returns {events, nextCursor}; each event is the webhook body (id, type, accountId, companyId, documentId, status, and externalReference, metadata, unvalidated, the message.mls fields and the message.outbound.ruleset_warning fields (ruleset, effectiveFrom, rules) when they apply) plus createdAt. id is the X-Peppol-Event-ID of the same event's webhook deliveries, so a client reading both deduplicates on it. nextCursor is always present: store it and ask again with ?after=; an empty page answers the same cursor back. Without ?after the feed starts at its oldest event. Events younger than 10 seconds are held back, so a page never skips one that commits late. ?type is one of the six event types, ?companyId narrows to one company, ?limit is at most 100 (default 50). A cursor this feed did not return is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. Confined to the companies the credential reaches.

Every file uploaded to out/ over SFTP for the companies this credential reaches, newest first, and what became of it — including the ones that were refused and so never became a message. Returns {files: [{id, accountId, companyId, companyName?, accountName?, path, fileName, sizeBytes, sha256, status, reason?, detail?, documentId?, attempts, createdAt, updatedAt}], nextCursor?}. status is queued (waiting, possibly after a transient failure that reason names), processing, sent (became a message and was filed under out/sent/; the message's own status says how far it got) or failed (filed under out/failed/). A failed file carries reason and detail, the same two things written to its .error.json; when it became a message that will not be sent — it failed validation — documentId names it too. path is relative to the account's SFTP root and is where the file was uploaded, not where it was moved. Filter with ?status (one of the four; anything else is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED), ?companyId, ?from and ?to (on createdAt); page with ?cursor and ?limit (default 50, at most 100).
One entry of GET /v1/files. A file of a company this credential does not reach is 404, like an id that does not exist.

post.description: Unauthenticated: {token, alternative?, signers}. Same as POST /v1/companies/{id}/kyc/signatories.
post.summary: Choose who signs, by onboarding link

post.description: Unauthenticated: {token, objectKey} or {token, manual: {…}}. Same validation and responses as POST /v1/companies/{id}/kyc.
post.summary: Start company KYC, by onboarding link

post.description: Unauthenticated: {token, size}. Same as POST /v1/companies/{id}/kyc/uploads for the link's company.
post.summary: Upload URL for a register extract, by onboarding link

post.description: Unauthenticated: {token} from a hosted onboarding link is the credential, for the one company it was issued for. Returns {company: {name, countryCode, registrationNumber}, kyc: …}, the same kyc object as GET /v1/companies/{id}/kyc. An unknown, replaced or expired link is 400 KYC_ONBOARDING_LINK_INVALID.
Unauthenticated: {token}. The case stays open; the company's owner can choose other signatories. 204.

Unauthenticated: {token, typedName, accept: true}. Records the signature with the time, the client address and user agent, and the agreement's SHA-256, consuming the token. When the signatures on the case bind the company under its firmateckning the case becomes VERIFIED; a case without a readable firmateckning goes to MANUAL_REVIEW once everyone asked has signed. Returns {status}, the case status afterwards. 400 KYC_SIGNING_LINK_INVALID as for view.
post.summary: Sign the agreement for a company

post.description: Unauthenticated: {token} from the mailed link is the credential, sent in the body so it never reaches an access log. Returns the company, the signer's name and role, the agreement version with its SHA-256, and a short-lived download url for the exact PDF being signed. An unknown, used, declined or expired token, or one whose case is no longer waiting for signatures, is 400 KYC_SIGNING_LINK_INVALID.

get.description: The signed-in user. session reports {authMethod: "password"|"sso", issuer, provider}, describing how they signed in; it is absent for an API key. Reachable even while user.mustChangePassword is true, when every other route is refused — so a client can tell why it is being refused. canViewBilling says whether GET /v1/billing will answer this caller: true for an owner, a user holding the billing.view grant, and a desk session; false for every API key. For a signed-in user, mfa is {enrolled, required, missing}: whether the user has an authenticator app, whether the account requires a second factor, and — when this session is held at that gate — which way out is left: "second-factor" (set up an app or a passkey) or "passkey-signin" (the user has a passkey and signed in with the password), "" otherwise. mfaEnrollmentRequired is true exactly when missing is set. Reachable while held at the gate.

Documents belonging to the companies this credential reaches; ?companyId narrows to one. ?q matches the sender and receiver participant from the start of the value, case-sensitively, or the document id exactly — never a substring in the middle. ?counts=true without an explicit ?from covers the last 30 days rather than the account's whole history. ?type is an alias from the register (invoice, credit-note, …), which names a document type and process together, or a raw documentTypeId. ?outcome is one of the statistics outcomes and stands for a set of statuses: delivered (AS4_ACCEPTED, CUSTOMER_DELIVERED), failed (SEND_FAILED, DISCOVERY_FAILED, REJECTED, VALIDATION_UNAVAILABLE, VALIDATION_ERROR, CUSTOMER_DELIVERY_FAILED), invalid (VALIDATION_FAILED, BUSINESS_INVALID), pending (every other status) and parked, which matches no document: a parked payload never became one. ?status still applies inside ?outcome. ?source is network or test. ?sandbox is exclude (leave sandbox companies' documents out), only (just theirs) or include (both, the default when it is absent). All four narrow ?counts=true and format=csv as well, so with the same from/to days, scope, type, outcome and source, and sandbox=exclude unless the statistics were asked with includeSandbox=true, its per-status counts add up to the statistics' count. ?direction is INBOUND or OUTBOUND, ?status one document status, ?delivery=pending the inbound documents not yet delivered to the customer. An unknown direction, status, delivery, outcome, source or sandbox value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming the values it takes; case is not significant. format=csv exports every document the filter matches, newest first, as one file — not one page: it reads the list page by page, up to 10000 rows. When the filter matches more, the answer carries X-Truncated: true and X-Next-Cursor; repeat the same request with ?cursor= set to that value for the next rows, until a response comes without the headers. ?limit and ?before do not apply to the export. ?externalReference= lists the documents with exactly that sender reference (case-sensitive, not unique: a resent invoice keeps its number); it is the last column of format=csv.

parameters.description: When true, the response gets a counts field breaking the active filter down by status/reason/eventType. limit=0 skips the rows and returns only counts.
parameters.name: counts

post.description: Optional externalReference (your own name for the document, at most 128 characters, compared exactly) and metadata (at most 16 string values, keys up to 40 characters, values up to 256) are stored and returned as given on GET /v1/messages/{id}, the lists and every webhook body about the document; outside those bounds the request is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. 202 with status QUEUED_VALIDATION is the usual answer: the document is checked against the Peppol rules after this request returns, not inside it, so the verdict is on a later GET rather than here: a passed document moves straight on to QUEUED and sending; VALIDATION_FAILED raises message.outbound.failed on the account's webhooks and is mailed to the company's notification contacts, with the findings on GET /v1/messages/{id}. VALIDATION_ERROR (a validator answer that cannot be read) and VALIDATION_UNAVAILABLE (no rules for the document and unvalidated sending not allowed) raise message.outbound.failed too, without the mail. A document type with no rules to check, sent under a capability that allows unvalidated documents, skips that step and is 201 with status UNVALIDATED: queued for sending like QUEUED, named so that the status says no rules were checked. A document whose rules the validator reports unavailable later becomes UNVALIDATED the same way when the capability allows it. A replayed Idempotency-Key is 200 with the current status. A key answers for 24 hours from its first use; after that it is unused, and the same key creates a new document. A payload that is a whole Standard Business Document is accepted: the envelope is taken off and the business document inside is what is stored and sent, under the platform's own SBDH. The envelope's sender, receiver, document type and process must then match the request's, or the request is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. type is a document type alias from the register (invoice, credit-note, order, …); pint-aunz-invoice and pint-aunz-credit-note are Peppol PINT A-NZ, the billing format for Australian and New Zealand receivers, whose documentTypeId is under the peppol-doctype-wildcard scheme rather than busdox-docid-qns. The business document must be what it is sent as: its root element and namespace, its cbc:CustomizationID (exactly) and, when present, its cbc:ProfileID must be the ones documentTypeId and processId name, or the request is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED before anything is stored — a BIS Billing 3.0 invoice sent as pint-aunz-invoice, a PINT invoice sent as invoice, a credit note sent as invoice. A documentTypeId ending in the wildcard indicator * matches no document (BR-PDW-02: * belongs in SMP registrations only). A document that states no CustomizationID among the root's children (CII, non-UBL) is not checked on that point. sender and receiver must both be among the business document's cbc:EndpointID values (schemeID:value; an organisation number written with a hyphen and a difference in case still match), or the request is 400 PARTY_MISMATCH before anything is stored, with a message naming the request's value and the document's endpoints. To send for a customer, send from the customer's own participant. A document that names no EndpointID (CII, non-UBL) is not checked on that point. Only sender and the payload are required. receiver left out is read off the document: the one cbc:EndpointID that is not the sender; a document that names no other party, or more than one (a delivery party, say), is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED asking for receiver. type, documentTypeId and processId all left out are read off the document as POST /v1/validate does — root element and namespace, cbc:CustomizationID and cbc:ProfileID — and a document that does not state them (CII, non-UBL) is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED asking for type. Whatever is stated is held to the document as above; the response's receiver, documentTypeId and processId say what was used. ?dryRun=true tries the send: every check above, by the same code, and then the Peppol validation the send would run later, inline — with nothing stored, queued or sent. The Idempotency-Key is neither looked up nor taken, and a payloadObjectKey upload is left in place, so the same request without dryRun is the real send. A refusal is the error and code the send would answer. Otherwise 200 {dryRun: true, companyId, sender, receiver, type, documentTypeId, processId, validated, valid, findings, ruleset, vesid, upcoming}, the findings, ruleset, vesid and upcoming as POST /v1/validate answers them: valid false is a document the send would accept and then fail as VALIDATION_FAILED. validated false and valid null is a type with no rules that its capability allows to go unvalidated. dryRun accepts only true or false; any other value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED and sends nothing. It shares POST /v1/validate's rate limit. ?wait=N (whole seconds, 0 to 30) holds the answer until the document's validation is decided, or N seconds pass: a verdict in time is 201 with that status (QUEUED, VALIDATION_FAILED, …), a wait that runs out the usual 202 QUEUED_VALIDATION, a replay 200 either way. Any other wait value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED and sends nothing. Two test receivers take a real send that never leaves the platform: 0007:0000000000 accepts it (AS4_ACCEPTED, then an MLS AP, recipientStatus CONFIRMED) and 0007:0000000018 rejects it (AS4_ACCEPTED, then an MLS RE with one BV issue). Name one as the document's buyer EndpointID. Every check and the validation run as usual; any sender may use them, a sandbox's local participants included; the document is source test and never billed.

200.description: A replayed Idempotency-Key (the document as it is now), or ?dryRun=true (DryRun).

201.description: Created with status UNVALIDATED (a type with no rules, under a capability that allows unvalidated documents), or ?wait= reached the validation verdict in time.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED, PARTY_MISMATCH, SENDER_NOT_FOUND, PEPPOL_LOCAL_PARTICIPANT, PEPPOL_DOCUMENT_NOT_SUPPORTED, NO_VALIDATION_RULES, PEPPOL_VALIDATION_FAILED

x-errors.when: The request is malformed or contradicts itself or the document: a bad field, an unknown JSON key, a type the document is not, an SBDH that disagrees, a receiver or type that could not be read off the document, or a payloadObjectKey that names no upload. Fix the request.
sender or receiver is not among the document's cbc:EndpointID values. Send from, and to, the parties the document names.
sender is not a participant under a company this credential reaches.
sender is a local test participant, which cannot send onto the Peppol network.
sender has no active SEND capability for this document type.
There are no validation rules for this document type, and its capability does not allow sending it unvalidated (allowUnvalidated).
The payload is unsafe XML (a DOCTYPE or an entity).
sender is not READY or ACTIVE yet. Retrying does not help until it is.
The Idempotency-Key was used before for a different request. A new document needs a new key.
The payload is over the inline limit (upload it, POST /v1/messages/uploads) or over PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES.
dryRun only: over POST /v1/validate's limit for this account (RateLimit-* headers). Wait Retry-After seconds. A send without dryRun is not rate limited.
Our failure. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key: a document that was created is replayed, not sent twice.
dryRun only: the validator's answer could not be read. The same document gets the same answer.
dryRun only: the validator is down. Retry later; a send without dryRun is queued and validated once it is back.

post.description: Body {bytes, sender?, companyId?}. sender is the participant the document will be sent from, as on POST /v1/messages: the upload is filed under that sender's company, which is where the send looks for it, so a caller reaching several companies needs no company id. companyId names the company directly; given both, they must agree (else 400 VALIDATION_FAILED); given neither, a caller reaching more than one company gets 400 COMPANY_REQUIRED. A sender outside the caller's companies is 400 SENDER_NOT_FOUND, as on the send. Answers {payloadObjectKey, uploadUrl, expiresAt, headers}. The uploadUrl is signed over Content-Type and Content-Length: PUT the document with exactly the headers in headers (Content-Type: application/xml) and a body of exactly bytes long, or the object store answers 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch. Then send the key with POST /v1/messages or check it with POST /v1/validate.

get.description: deliveryUnconfirmed is true on an outbound SEND_FAILED message whose send outcome the platform could not learn: the receiver may already have it, and it is never resent. Show it as unconfirmed rather than failed, and do not resend it either. mlsEvents lists the Peppol Message Level Status trail, oldest first. An entry with direction INBOUND and status RECEIVED is an MLS the receiving Service Provider sent about this outbound message: responseCode is AP (delivered with confirmation), AB (delivered without) or RE (rejected); description is its text; issues is its line responses [{location, reasonCode, description}] with reasonCode SV, BV, BW or FD, and reasons their distinct codes; receivedAt, mlsId and sender (the SP's 0242 participant) identify it. A message's own status does not change on an MLS. Entries with direction OUTBOUND (PENDING/SENT/FAILED/SKIPPED) are history from before 2026-10-08 and carry none of these fields. The message.mls webhook carries mlsEventId, responseCode, reasons and issues for the entry it announces. recipientStatus, on an outbound message once the receiving Service Provider's MLS has arrived, is that status in one word: CONFIRMED (AP, delivered with confirmation), DELIVERED (AB, delivered without) or REJECTED (RE), with recipientStatusReasons the distinct reason codes of a rejection. Outbound documents ask for a status on every send (MLS_TYPE=ALWAYS_SEND), but a receiving Service Provider that does not support MLS sends none, so an absent recipientStatus means no answer, not a failure. validation {ruleset, vesid, validatedAt} says which Peppol rules decided the message's validation status: the release in force when it was submitted (outbound) or received (inbound), not when it was checked, so a message submitted the day before a new release becomes mandatory is judged by the old one. Absent while it has not been validated, for a type with no rules, and for messages validated before 2026-11-24. validation.upcoming {ruleset, vesid, effectiveFrom, valid, findings} is an outbound message checked against the release scheduled next, shown until that release takes effect: a forecast that never changes the message's status. When valid is false, message.outbound.ruleset_warning was raised for it.

delete.description: Body {currentPassword}. Turns the signed-in user's two-factor off and discards their recovery codes; sessions stay signed in. 400 CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED or CURRENT_PASSWORD_INVALID, 409 MFA_NOT_ENROLLED when it is not on, 429 RATE_LIMITED after repeated wrong passwords. When the account requires two-factor, the next request is held at the gate until a new factor is set up: this is how a user moves to a new phone. 403 FORBIDDEN for credentials without a person.

post.description: Body {code} from the app. Turns two-factor on and answers {recoveryCodes}: ten one-time codes, shown this once and never again, each of which stands in for an app code once. Every other session of the user is signed out; this one stays. 400 MFA_CODE_INVALID for a wrong code, 409 MFA_NOT_ENROLLED without POST /v1/mfa/enroll first, 409 MFA_ALREADY_ENROLLED when it is already on, 429 RATE_LIMITED after repeated wrong codes. Reachable while held at the gate. 403 FORBIDDEN for credentials without a person, as above.

Answers {secret, otpauthUrl} for the signed-in user; show otpauthUrl as a QR code. Nothing is turned on until POST /v1/mfa/confirm, and calling this again replaces the secret. 409 MFA_ALREADY_ENROLLED when an app is already on; turn it off first. Reachable while the account's two-factor requirement holds the session at the gate. An API key, a desk session and an OIDC bearer get 403 FORBIDDEN: an authenticator app belongs to a person.

{companyId?, ids: ["scheme:value", ...]}, at most 100 ids (400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming the cap above that, or on an empty list). Looked up concurrently, capped at 8 against SMP. Returns {results: [{id, status: OK|INVALID|ERROR, canonicalId?, exists?, smpUrl?, capabilities?, testReceiver?, error?}]}, one entry per id in the same order, even when some ids fail: INVALID is a malformed id (no SMP call made), ERROR is a failed SMP call, and OK carries exists (false is a normal, common answer, not an error). A test receiver (0007:0000000000, 0007:0000000018) answers exists:true with the invoice and credit-note capabilities, no smpUrl and testReceiver:true: it is on no SMP and is answered without one.

get.description: ?q is either a full Peppol id, looked up exactly (response mode "id"), or free text tried as a national registration number against every scheme we know a format rule for and, where the Peppol Directory is available, as a name or number query against it (mode "search"). Search results are confirmed hits only: a candidate that does not parse, is not registered, or returns no Directory match all give zero rows rather than a not-found entry — unlike "id" mode, whose exists:false is definitive, a search miss only means this route did not find them. directoryConfigured says whether the Directory was consulted, so an empty result can be explained as "they may simply never have published a business card". A test receiver (0007:0000000000, 0007:0000000018) answers exists:true with the invoice and credit-note capabilities, no smpUrl and testReceiver:true: it is on no SMP and is answered without one. The search answers both, named, for q "test", "test receiver(s)" or "testmottagare".
get.summary: Search counterparties by name or national number

get.description: {exists, canonicalId, smpUrl, capabilities, testReceiver?}. exists:false is definitive: the id is not registered on Peppol. A test receiver (0007:0000000000, 0007:0000000018) answers exists:true with the invoice and credit-note capabilities, no smpUrl and testReceiver:true: it is on no SMP and is answered without one.

{capabilities: [documentTypeId, ...]} the participant is registered to receive. A test receiver (0007:0000000000, 0007:0000000018) answers exists:true with the invoice and credit-note capabilities, no smpUrl and testReceiver:true: it is on no SMP and is answered without one.

Every participant under the companies the principal reaches; ?companyId narrows to one of them. ?status and ?q (scheme:value, canonicalId, name, identifier) filter in memory like the admin list. ?counts=true adds a status breakdown for the account (scoped by companyId when given). An unknown status, direction or category value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming the values the parameter takes; case is not significant.

parameters.description: When true, the response gets a counts field breaking the active filter down by status/reason/eventType. limit=0 skips the rows and returns only counts.
parameters.name: counts

post.description: Optional capabilities: an array of {documentTypeId, processId, direction, allowUnvalidated}, the same element shape as POST /v1/participants/{id}/capabilities, document type aliases included ({"type": "invoice"} or {"documentTypeId": "invoice"}). Created in the same transaction as the participant. Omitted = no capabilities, matching pre-existing behaviour. A Peppol id another live participant holds, on any account, is 409 CONFLICT; one whose participant is DEACTIVATED is free to register again (DEACTIVATING still holds it until the SMP entry is gone).

delete.description: On any status but DEACTIVATED it deactivates and returns the participant: one with anything in SMP becomes DEACTIVATING and stays published for the unpublish grace, anything else becomes DEACTIVATED. On a participant already DEACTIVATED it deletes it instead and answers 204 No Content: the participant leaves every list and count, GET /v1/participants/{id} answers 404, and its identifier is free again in its company. Calling DELETE until it answers 204 therefore takes a participant all the way off. The deletion is soft — documents, usage and billing keep pointing at it — and is audited as PARTICIPANT_DELETED. Participant responses carry deletedAt, always null on the customer API.

get.description: Filter with ?eventType, ?q (substring over actor and metadata), ?from/?to. Each row carries actorName and, where the event has one, targetType/targetId/targetName/targetSub (A8) — no targetHref, since this surface has no admin pages to link a company/account/login target to. An unknown status, direction or category value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming the values the parameter takes; case is not significant.

delete.description: Drops the stored card; the default built from the company's name and country is republished. Answers that default (custom false). A no-op when no card is stored. Audited as BUSINESS_CARD_DELETED.

get.description: The business card published to the Peppol Directory for this participant: {participantId, custom, entities: [{names: [{name, language?}], countryCode, geographicalInformation?, identifiers: [{scheme, value}], websites: [url], contacts: [{type?, name?, phoneNumber?, email?}], additionalInformation?, registrationDate?}]}. custom is false when no card has been set and entities is the default built from the company's name and country — what is published until a card is PUT.

put.description: Replaces the whole card with {entities: [...]} (participantId and custom are accepted and ignored, so a GET response can be sent back as is) and queues it for republishing. At least one entity, each with at least one name (at most 256 characters); countryCode is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; language a two- or three-letter ISO 639 code; registrationDate YYYY-MM-DD; websites absolute http(s) URLs; email a bare address; at most 20 entities, 10 names, 20 identifiers, 10 websites and 20 contacts per entity. Anything else is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming the field. Answers the stored card, same shape as GET. Audited as BUSINESS_CARD_UPDATED. Published only while the participant is ACTIVE on the network.

post.description: {documentTypeId, processId, direction, allowUnvalidated} with canonical Peppol identifiers, or a document type alias as on POST /v1/messages: {type: "invoice", direction} — or the alias as documentTypeId with no processId. Stored canonical; an unknown alias, or a type that contradicts the ids given with it, is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

get.description: {passkeys:[{id, name, aaguid, transports, createdAt, lastUsedAt}]} for the signed-in user. An API key has no passkeys and gets 403: a passkey belongs to a person, not to an account.

post.description: {name, id, attestationObject, clientDataJSON, transports}, the binary members base64url. The challenge must be one issued to this same user, and must not have been used already.

Returns {publicKey}: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions for the signed-in user, with their existing credentials in excludeCredentials so one authenticator cannot hold two passkeys for the same account.

delete.description: Removing the last one is allowed and needs no confirmation: every user always has a password, so a passkey is an alternative sign-in method rather than the only one.

get.summary: SFTP connection details (host, port, host key fingerprint, per-login root and layout, file settings)

get.description: A credential confined to particular companies sees only the logins belonging to them; a login with no company reaches the whole account and is visible only to credentials that do too. ?companyId narrows to one company; an account-wide login stays in view whichever company is asked for.

patch.description: {resetPassword: true} and nothing else: the new password is in the response, once. Changing the authentication method, disabling a login, setting a password directly or moving it between companies is 400 OPERATOR_MANAGED — ask us instead. Owner or company admin, the latter only for a login belonging to one of its own companies.

post.description: Session principal or API key. For a session, the token's email must match the caller's own account email or the request is refused with 400 SSO_EMAIL_MISMATCH — an API key has no user to match against and keeps the unrestricted automation path.

delete.description: An owner may remove any identity in the account; any other signed-in user only one whose email is their own (403 FORBIDDEN otherwise); an API key keeps the account-wide automation path.

get.description: Unauthenticated: {configured, provider, issuer, passkeysEnabled}, so a sign-in page can show or hide the single sign-on button, and label it with the right provider name, before anyone has signed in.

Metered events for the caller's account in [from, to) (default: the last 24 hours): totals per kind and the same per company, for re-billing. ?companyId narrows to one company the principal reaches; format=csv exports accountId,companyId,kind,count.

Owner or company admin. An owner sees every user under the account; a company admin sees only the users whose companies lie entirely inside its own, plus itself. ?companyId narrows to the users who reach that company; a user with no confinement reaches every company and stays in view. Every user carries status ("active" | "inactive"); a deactivated one also carries disabledAt, and erasableAt once it can be erased. Only active users are listed unless ?include=inactive; any other value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. Every user carries grants, the rights stored for them on top of their role (today only "billing.view"); it is always an array, and always empty for an owner, who holds every grant implicitly. mfaEnrolled says whether the user has an authenticator app turned on, and passkeyCount how many passkeys they hold (DELETE /v1/users/{id}/passkeys removes them).

post.description: Owner or company admin. role is one of owner, company_admin, member. companyIds confines the user to those companies; from an owner, empty means every company, an owner can never be confined, and a company admin must name at least one. A company admin may create only a member or another company admin, only within its own companies, and an omitted companyIds then means its own companies rather than the whole account. Leave password out: a random one is generated, the user is flagged mustChangePassword, and a one-time set-password link is emailed. If mail is not available, temporaryPassword comes back once instead, for you to hand over another way.

delete.description: Owner or company admin, the latter only for a user inside its own companies. The first call deactivates: sign-in is refused, sessions and passkeys are deleted, and status becomes "inactive". The last active owner cannot be deactivated (409 LAST_OWNER), nor can you deactivate yourself (400 VALIDATION_FAILED). After the user has stayed deactivated for the grace period — 30 days — a second call erases them permanently instead; 409 USER_NOT_DISABLED, ERASURE_TOO_SOON and ERASURE_NOT_CONFIGURED name the cases where it will not. POST /v1/users/{id}/enable reverses a deactivation.

patch.description: Changing your own password requires currentPassword: wrong is 400 CURRENT_PASSWORD_INVALID, missing is 400 CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED. It is not required when an owner resets somebody else's. Setting your own password while signed in through single sign-on is refused with 403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_SSO_SESSION. On your own id this is one of the two routes still reachable while mustChangePassword is true, and setting a real password clears the flag without a fresh sign-in. role and companyIds need an owner, or a company admin acting on someone else — never on your own row, so nobody widens their own access. companyIds replaces the user's confinement; omitted leaves it alone, and from an owner, empty means every company. Promoting someone to owner always clears it. A change takes effect on the user's next request. resendInvite is the sibling of resetPassword for a user who never set a password: it mails a 48-hour invitation link rather than the one-hour reset link. grants replaces the user's grants — today only "billing.view", the right to read GET /v1/billing; omitted leaves them alone and [] takes them all away. Only an owner gives grants (403 FORBIDDEN for a company admin, a member and every API key); an owner holds them all implicitly, so a non-empty grants on an owner, and an unknown grant, are 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

post.description: Owner or company admin, the latter only for a user inside its own companies. The user signs in again with the password they already had and keeps the companies they had; deactivation never touched either. Passkeys do not come back — deactivation deleted them — so a new one has to be registered. API keys are unaffected either way: a key belongs to the account, not to whoever created it, and is revoked on its own. Reactivating an already-active user is not an error.

delete.description: Owner only: the way back for a user who lost both phone and recovery codes. Turns the user's two-factor off without their password, discards their recovery codes and signs out every session they hold; passkeys stay. They sign in again with their password, and when the account requires two-factor they are asked to set up a new factor. 403 FORBIDDEN for anyone but an owner — a company admin included — and for API keys and desk sessions; 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on your own id (use DELETE /v1/mfa with your password); 404 for a user not in this account; 409 MFA_NOT_ENROLLED when the user has no app.

Owner only: the way back for a user who signs in with a passkey and lost the device. Removes every passkey the user holds and signs out every session they hold; their password and authenticator app stay. They sign in again with their password, and when the account requires two-factor and they have no authenticator app they are asked to set one up or register a new passkey. Works whether or not passkeys are configured on this deployment. 403 FORBIDDEN for anyone but an owner — a company admin included — and for API keys and desk sessions; 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on your own id (use DELETE /v1/passkeys/{id}); 404 for a user not in this account; 409 INVALID_STATE when the user has no passkeys.

post.description: Runs a document through the same Peppol validation an outbound message gets — XML safety, then XSD and Schematron in the validator — and answers every finding, warnings included. Nothing is stored and nothing is sent. Body {type?, documentTypeId?, processId?, payload} or, for a document over the 1 MiB JSON body limit, {payloadObjectKey, sender? or companyId?} naming an upload from POST /v1/messages/uploads and the sender or company it was uploaded with; the upload is read and left in place, so the same key can be sent next. type is an alias ("invoice", …); with neither type nor ids the identifiers are read off the document (root element, CustomizationID, ProfileID). A stated type the document contradicts (as POST /v1/messages would refuse with 400) is answered here as the first finding — severity fatal, rule DOCUMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH, no layer — followed by the validator's own, with valid false. Answers {valid, documentTypeId, processId, type, findings: [{severity, rule, location, message, layer}]}: valid is false only on a fatal finding; layer "schema" means the document is not valid UBL and Schematron did not run. ruleset and vesid say what the answer was reached under: the Peppol release in force now ("2026.5") and the exact validation artefacts the validator ran; Peppol publishes a new release twice a year, each mandatory from a set date, and the answer changes with it. While a release is scheduled, upcoming {ruleset, vesid, effectiveFrom, valid, findings} is the same document checked against it: what it will meet from effectiveFrom. ?ruleset=NAME checks against one release from GET /v1/validation/rulesets instead, in force or scheduled, and answers no upcoming; any other name is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. 400 PEPPOL_DOCUMENT_NOT_SUPPORTED for a type without artefacts, 400 PEPPOL_VALIDATION_FAILED for unsafe XML, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE for an upload over PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES, 404 for a company the credential does not reach, 503 VALIDATION_UNAVAILABLE while the validator is down. Rate limited per account, 120 a minute shared with dry runs: every answer carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset (seconds until the oldest call in the window leaves it), and a refusal is 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After.
post.summary: Validate a document without sending it

get.description: Unauthenticated. Peppol publishes its validation rules as releases, twice a year, each mandatory from a date announced months ahead. Answers {rulesets: [{name, title, effectiveFrom, status}]}, oldest first: the release in force (status in_force) and any scheduled after it (status scheduled), effectiveFrom being when it takes effect (RFC 3339 UTC; absent on a release in force from the start). A message is validated under the release in force when it was submitted or received; name is what validation.ruleset on GET /v1/messages/{id}, ruleset on POST /v1/validate and ?ruleset= use. Cached for five minutes.
get.summary: Peppol validation releases in force and scheduled

get.description: A credential confined to particular companies sees only the endpoints belonging to them. An endpoint with no company receives events for the whole account and is visible only to credentials that reach it. ?companyId narrows to one company; an account-wide endpoint stays in view whichever company is asked for.

post.description: Owner, company admin, or an API key with manage. companyId confines the endpoint to one company's documents; leaving it out sends every company under the account to it, which only an owner or an account-wide key may create. A key confined to one company manages that company's endpoints only. Payloads carry accountId and companyId, so one endpoint can serve many companies. The endpoint URL must be https://; an http:// URL is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (only a local development deployment accepts it). The signing secret is returned once, here.

put.description: Same body and access as POST /v1/webhooks, made idempotent for a platform that registers its endpoint on every deploy. An endpoint with the same URL and companyId is updated in place — enabled, timeoutMs, and the secret only when one is given — and answered 200 with created: false and no secret. Otherwise one is created and answered 201 with created: true and the signing secret, exactly as POST. A URL that changes is a new endpoint; delete the old one. A new endpoint must be https://, as for POST; an existing http:// endpoint can still be updated in place.
put.summary: Create or update a webhook by endpoint URL

get.description: Deliveries for the principal's account (companyFilter applies). Filter with ?status, ?companyId, ?from, ?to; page with ?cursor and ?limit. Returns {deliveries, nextCursor?}. An unknown status, direction or category value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming the values the parameter takes; case is not significant.

post.description: Sends a DEAD_LETTER delivery again, now, with the same X-Peppol-Event-ID, type and body; the normal retry schedule follows if it fails again. Find them with GET /v1/webhooks/deliveries?status=DEAD_LETTER. Needs manage. 409 INVALID_STATE for a delivery that is not a dead letter (still pending or retrying, delivered, cancelled), whose webhook is disabled, or whose company is closed. 404 for an id outside the caller's companies. Audit-logged as WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_RETRIED.

delete.description: Owner, company admin, or an API key with manage, with the same rule about which endpoints it reaches as PATCH.

patch.description: Owner, company admin, or an API key with manage — a company admin or a company-confined key only for an endpoint belonging to its own companies. A changed endpoint must be https://; an existing http:// endpoint keeps its URL unless it is replaced by an https:// one. rotateSecret, or a new secret, issues a new signing secret and returns it once. X-Peppol-Signature uses the new secret from the next attempt on; for 24 hours the replaced secret also signs every delivery in X-Peppol-Signature-Previous, so the new one can be rolled out to every verifier without dropping calls, and the response carries previousSecretExpiresAt. A second rotation inside the window replaces the overlap. expirePreviousSecret: true ends the overlap at once (with rotateSecret in the same request, the rotation has none) — for a secret replaced because it leaked.
